title: Add region health aggregator service (API + routing integration stubs)
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Internal-only: introduces Region Health Service used by failover controller/routing (behind flags). No customer-visible API changes.
body: Summary: This PR adds the initial implementation of the Region Health Service (RHS): a small control-plane service that aggregates multiple signal streams into a single cached health view per region, per product surface (Hosted API vs Dedicated), and per routing "route class" (chat/generate/embeddings). This is a foundational building block for the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade; routing and the failover controller will consume RHS rather than each team independently interpreting raw metrics. Scope in this PR is intentionally limited to: (1) ingest + aggregate a minimal set of signals, (2) expose a stable internal API, (3) ship tests and canned fixtures, and (4) add integration stubs for routing/policy evaluation behind a feature flag. Motivation / context: Today our failover decisioning pulls from several places (burn alerts, reachability probes, ad-hoc dashboards) and the interpretation differs across Hosted vs Dedicated paths. During staging rehearsals we’ve also seen missing/late signals cause inconsistent decisions or controller crashes. RHS provides a single, defensive, typed interface with explicit freshness requirements and a "degraded vs unknown" distinction. This PR is a prerequisite for deterministic trigger hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042) and for building safe automation + rollback guardrails (ADR-043). Design highlights: Aggregation model: RHS evaluates region health as a set of per-signal observations + a computed status. Status is one of {HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNHEALTHY, UNKNOWN}. UNKNOWN is reserved for cases where we cannot produce a trustworthy view (e.g., missing reachability feed + stale metrics), and is intended to be treated as "do not auto-failover" by the controller unless corroborated elsewhere. Signals included in this first cut: (a) reachability probe status from perf-canary (cross-region HTTP + TCP probe), (b) service-level 5xx burn (1m/5m rolling) from the SLO metrics pipeline, (c) tail latency burn (p95/p99 vs SLO target) from the same pipeline, (d) capacity headroom placeholder (stubbed interface; returns UNKNOWN until ENG-2414 lands), (e) control-plane dependency check (basic: routing config store + policy engine RPC health). Freshness + caching: RHS caches computed health views for 5s with jitter (±20%) to avoid stampedes during partial outages. Each signal includes last_updated_at and a max_age budget; if any required signal exceeds its max_age the final status becomes UNKNOWN (unless an authoritative reachability failure is present). API (internal): GET /internal/v1/region-health?surface=hosted|dedicated&region=us-east&route_class=chat returns the computed health, per-signal observations, and a "reason_summary" string intended for audit logs. GET /internal/v1/region-health/summary?surface=hosted returns all regions for that surface in one response to support controller loops. Note: This is internal-only (mTLS + service auth); no external customer endpoints. Observability: Exposes rhs_cache_hit_total, rhs_compute_latency_ms, rhs_signal_staleness_seconds{signal=...}, rhs_region_status{surface,region,route_class,status}. Logging is structured with request_id and evaluation_id so routing/controller can reference exact computations in their own audit events later. Integration stubs: Adds a RegionHealthClient in routing/policy-engine with a disabled-by-default path (feature flag: routing.region_health.enabled=false). When enabled, routing fetches RHS summary on a background ticker and stores it in memory for policy evaluation predicates (currently predicate returns "unknown" unless explicitly enabled; no routing decisions change in production as part of this PR). Tests: Unit tests: coverage for status computation, freshness handling, and precedence rules (reachability failure overrides stale error metrics; stale required signals yield UNKNOWN). Integration tests: spins up RHS with fake signal providers (fixtures) and asserts the API output schema + caching behavior. Contract-ish test: small routing-side test that ensures the client handles partial/missing fields and timeouts without crashing (returns UNKNOWN). Security / safety: RHS has explicit timeouts for each upstream signal provider and fails closed to UNKNOWN instead of inferring HEALTHY from missing data. Rate limiting: internal per-caller QPS limit (configurable) to prevent controller/routing thundering herd. AuthZ: restricted to allowlisted service identities (routing, failover-controller, incident-bot in later PR). Rollout plan: Land RHS as a standalone service in staging first; routing integration is present but disabled. Follow-ups: (1) ENG-2414 integrate real capacity headroom signal provider; (2) ENG-2417 wire reachability probes as first-class ingestion rather than polling; (3) PR to add cache TTL tuning based on observed load (likely 2s-10s); (4) formalize schema versioning once controller consumes it; (5) add dashboard panels for rhs_region_status and staleness. Commits (squash summary): 1) region-health-service: skeleton service + config wiring; 2) rhs: signal provider interfaces + aggregation engine; 3) rhs: internal HTTP API handlers + auth; 4) routing: add RegionHealthClient (flagged) + predicate stub; 5) tests: fixtures + integration harness; 6) obs: metrics + structured logs; 7) docs: internal README + runbook stub. Changed areas (high-level): services/region-health-service/* (new) for service code and deployment manifests; pkg/regionhealth/* for shared types; routing/policy-engine/* for client + predicate stub (flagged); deploy/helm/* adds chart and default values for staging; tests/integration/region-health-service/* adds fixture-based tests. Reviewer discussion (highlights): Ravi Menon: asked for a hard stance on UNKNOWN semantics and how routing should treat it. Resolution: added explicit docstring and a unit test that UNKNOWN does not imply healthy; routing predicate now requires explicit enablement + non-UNKNOWN to be used. Allison Grant: flagged metric label cardinality risk if we include tenant identifiers. Resolution: no tenant dimensions added; surface/region/route_class only, plus a note in README for future additions. Victor Alvarez: requested clarity on reachability probe sources and how to distinguish provider DNS issues vs regional impairment. Resolution: added probe_source and probe_type fields internally (not labels) and improved reason_summary string to include "reachability:tcp_fail" vs "reachability:http_5xx". Jordan Lee: asked for deterministic ordering of reasons to support audit logs. Resolution: reason_summary now uses a stable ordering and includes the evaluation_id. CI: build/test/lint all green after rerunning integration tests once (flaky due to clock mocking; fixed by using monotonic test clock). Checks: //ci/redwood:unit-tests PASS, //ci/redwood:integration-tests PASS, //ci/redwood:lint PASS, //ci/redwood:container-build PASS. Merge: Squash merged into main after approvals from routing + observability + network.
